sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.9 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth was front-loaded: 64.2% in FY2021 [D218], then 11.8% in FY2022 [D263] and 0.1% in FY2023 [D311], before recovering to 16.4% in FY2024 [D358] and 10.6% in FY2025 [D406].
FY2017's operating loss of $3.5 billion [F12] came from a $2.6 billion stock-based compensation charge tied to RSUs whose performance condition was satisfied at IPO [P74].
The operating margin improved 5.7pp in FY2025 [D419], reaching -9.0% [F30] from -14.7% in FY2024 [F29].
North America still supplies 58.6% of revenue [D456] but contributed only 4.4pp of FY2025's 10.6% growth [D458][D406].
Rest of world grew 17.0% and added 3.7pp [D498][D499], while Europe added 2.5pp on 14.1% growth [D523][D524].
Advertising revenue rose 5.8% and added 5.3pp [D537][D538], on roughly 17% more impressions offset by a 10% lower cost per impression [P24].
Other revenue grew 62.9% and added 5.4pp [D544][D545], driven by higher subscription revenue from subscriber growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth [D423][D406], an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D429].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% [F30] is the window high, against a median of -32.4% [D555] and a low of -422.5% [D553].
Cost of revenue fell to 45.0% of revenue from 46.1% [D386][D338], adding 1.1pp to margin [D431].
R&D fell to 30.2% of revenue from 31.6% [D387][D339], adding 1.3pp [D432], and selling and marketing fell to 17.2% from 19.8% [D388][D340].
The sales and marketing decline came from the timing of marketing events, lower advertising investment and $19.9 million of prior-year restructuring charges [P22].
Net margin of -7.8% [F50] was helped by $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains in other income [P18].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million [F80] was 1.4x the $460.5 million net loss [F40], and free cash flow reached $437.2 million [F100], a 7.4% margin [D393].
The gap is non-cash: stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion and depreciation and amortization of $163.6 million [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue [F90][D392] and 1.34x D&A [D395], up from a 4.1% free-cash-flow margin in FY2024 [D345].
Capex is mainly improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces [P10].
Cash and investments of $2.9 billion against $3.5 billion of debt [D397][D398] leaves net debt of $596.3 million [D399], equal to 10.1% of revenue [D400].
That ranks at the 0th percentile against internet peers, whose median net cash is 45.0% of revenue (n=5) [D578][D579].
The company issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of 2026-2028 notes in February 2025 [P2][P1].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow [D401][D402], while the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D425].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years [R1], from $514.6 million in FY2016 [F31] to $460.5 million in FY2025 [F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 [D390] and has stayed above 10% for nine years [R2], equal to 191.1% of the operating loss [D404].
Net cash has fallen for four straight years, from $1.4 billion in FY2021 [D211] to net debt of $596.3 million [D399][R3].
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R4], reaching 171.7% in FY2025 [D402].
Operating margin: a FY2026 reading above the FY2025 high of -9.0% [D554] would confirm the leverage trend; a slip back toward the -32.4% median [D555] would reverse it.
Free cash flow margin: holding above the FY2025 7.4% [D560] confirms the cash trend; falling below the -4.1% median [D561] would not.
Net cash: any move back above zero from -$596.3 million [D399] would reverse the four-year deterioration, reported in the FY2026 10-K.
